title: A fixed Cohen presentation lifts to a local power-series evaluation square
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ and $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $r:R	woheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective local homomorphism. Local means that the source maximal ideal maps into the target maximal ideal. Let $p\ge0$ be the characteristic of $A/\mathfrak m_A$. Fix $n\ge0$ and a ring $\Lambda$, a characteristic-zero field if $p=0$, and a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ if $p>0$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Put $T_0=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and fix a surjective local homomorphism $c_0:T_0	woheadrightarrow A$. For every finite tuple $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ generating $J=\ker r$, including $s=0$ when $J=0$, put $T=T_0[[y_1,\ldots,y_s]]$, identify it with $\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_s]]$ by regrouping coefficients, and let $\pi:T	o T_0$ take the constant coefficient in the $y$ variables. Then $T_0,T$ are complete regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme], with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_\Lambda T_0+(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and $\mathfrak m_\Lambda T+(x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$ respectively, and $\pi$ is surjective local. There exist local ring homomorphisms $f:T_0	o R$ and $h:T	o R$ such that $rf=c_0$, $h|_{T_0}=f$, $h(y_j)=b_j$, and $rh=c_0\pi$. For every $F=\sum_
u a_
u y^
u\in T$ and $N\ge1$ they satisfy
$$h(F)\equiv\sum_{|
u|<N}f(a_
u)b^
u\pmod{\mathfrak m_R^N},\qquad |
u|=\sum_j
u_j,\quad b^
u=\prod_j b_j^{
u_j}.$$
No surjectivity of $h$ is asserted.

proof.text:
By the coefficient-family definition, regrouping a family indexed by $(\alpha,
u)\in\mathbf N^n	imes\mathbf N^s$ gives a ring isomorphism $\Lambda[[x,y]]\cong T_0[[y]]$: addition agrees coefficientwise, and the product coefficient at $(\alpha,
u)$ is the same finite sum over $(\alpha_1,
u_1)+(\alpha_2,
u_2)=(\alpha,
u)$. The inclusion of $T_0$ is constant in $y$. Taking the coefficient at $
u=0$ is a ring map $\pi$ with this inclusion as a section, hence is surjective. These statements include empty index sets.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, first and third paragraphs; the lifted square before the subsequent surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply the field/Cohen power-series theorem over $\Lambda$ with $d=n$ and $d=n+s$. Through step 1 this gives exactly the asserted completeness, regular locality, and maximal-ideal formulas for $T_0$ and $T$. The map $\pi$ sends every coefficient-maximal-ideal generator into $\mathfrak m_\Lambda T_0$, every $x_i$ into $\mathfrak m_{T_0}$, and every $y_j$ to zero. Thus it maps $\mathfrak m_T$ into $\mathfrak m_{T_0}$ and is local.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, first and third paragraphs; the lifted square before the subsequent surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: Put $J=\ker r$. For $u\in J$, the element $u$ cannot be a unit since $r(u)=0$ in the nonzero local ring $A$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$. To check closedness, if $u\in\bigcap_{N\ge1}(J+\mathfrak m_R^N)$, locality of $r$ gives $r(u)\in\mathfrak m_A^N$ for every $N$. Completeness includes $\bigcap_N\mathfrak m_A^N=0$, hence $u\in J$. The reverse inclusion is immediate. Therefore $J=\bigcap_N(J+\mathfrak m_R^N)$. Identify $R/J$ with $A$ by $[u]\mapsto r(u)$; this is bijective by surjectivity of $r$ and the definition of $J$.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, first and third paragraphs; the lifted square before the subsequent surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: The field/Cohen formal-smoothness lemma says that $\mathbf Z\to T_0$ is formally smooth for $\mathfrak m_{T_0}$ in both allowed cases. Apply the complete-target lifting lemma over $\mathbf Z$, with its source $S=T_0$, target $R$ (called $A$ in that lemma), ideal of definition $I=\mathfrak m_R$, closed kernel $J$, and quotient map $g=c_0:T_0\to R/J\cong A$. All ring maps are $\mathbf Z$-linear. We have $J^1\subseteq I$ by step 3. Also $g(\mathfrak m_{T_0})\subseteq q(I)$: if $a\in\mathfrak m_A$, any lift $u$ under $r$ is a nonunit, since a unit has unit image, hence $u\in I$. In particular this holds for $a=c_0(z)$ with $z\in\mathfrak m_{T_0}$. Take the lemma's integers $t=r=1$. Its conclusion supplies $f:T_0\to R$ with $rf=c_0$ and $f(\mathfrak m_{T_0})\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$, the required locality.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, first and third paragraphs; the lifted square before the subsequent surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: Every $b_j$ lies in $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$. Apply adic power-series evaluation with coefficient ring $C=T_0$, coefficient map $\alpha=f$, target $R$, ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, and variables $y_1,\ldots,y_s$. This gives a ring map $h:T_0[[y]]\to R$ restricting to $f$, with $h(y_j)=b_j$, and with precisely the displayed congruence for every $F$ and $N\ge1$. By step 2 the maximal ideal of $T$ is generated by $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$, the $x_i$, and the $y_j$. The images of the first two groups lie in $f(\mathfrak m_{T_0})\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$ and those of the last group are the $b_j$. Consequently $h$ is local.

source.place: Tag 09PZ (lemma-ci-well-defined), proof, first and third paragraphs; the lifted square before the subsequent surjectivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply $r$ to the congruence of step 5. It sends $\mathfrak m_R^N$ into $\mathfrak m_A^N$. Every term with $|\nu|>0$ vanishes because $r(b_j)=0$, and the constant term becomes $r(f(a_0))=c_0(a_0)$. Hence $rh(F)-c_0\pi(F)\in\mathfrak m_A^N$ for every $N\ge1$. The separatedness included in completeness of $A$ makes this difference zero, proving $rh=c_0\pi$. If $s=0$, evaluation is just $h=f$ and $\pi$ is the identity; if $n=0$ the same arguments start with $T_0=\Lambda$. Nothing here requires any surjectivity property of $h$.
